To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the enhancement by US on electrochemical oxidation on BDD is greater than for Pt; the variety of intermediaries produced on BDD in the absence of US is less than for on Pt; in the presence of US no change occurred to amounts of the intermediates species; the time for intermediates reaching the highest concentration on both electrodes is cut down by US, the effect for degradation of phenol on BDD is better than on Pt.
the electrochemical oxidation of Ph on BBD is enhanced by the application of US and the mechanism and kinetics of the process is different from that of Pt.
the enhancement of ultrasound on electrochemical oxidation of Ph is much greater for BDD than for Pt.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the ultrasound-enhanced electro-oxidation of phenol on BDD electrode.
the mechanism and kinetics of US enhanced electrochemical oxidation for Ph on BDD and Pt electrodes.
the mechanism of US enhanced electrochemical degradation of Ph on boron-dopped diamond and Pt electrodes and kinetics of the intermediates produced during the process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
US enhanced electrochemical oxidation is an attractive method for degradation of organic contaminants in water.
the degradation of phenol on BDD by ultrasound enhanced electrochemical oxidation is more efficient than on Pt.

the US enhanced electrochemical oxidation on BDD electrode has a higher degradation rate and current yield than on Pt, and the degradation rate is increased by 301%, while the current efficiency is increased by 100%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the US enhanced electrochemical oxidation is an effective method to remove organic pollutants.
the enhancement of the electrochemical reaction by US is caused by a combination of factors including mass transfer, adsorption and electrode reaction.
US can enhance the efficiency and rate of electrochemical oxidation of Ph by increasing the amount of intermediates produced and the rate of their generation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
US enhanced electrochemical oxidation on BDD can degrade Ph effectively and the mechanism is quite different from that on Pt.
the use of ultrasound can enhance the degradation rate of phenol on the boron-doped electrode.
the BDD is a good material for the electro-oxidation of organic pollutants in the presence of US.
